question.problem: Consider the positively (outward) oriented surface $S$ given by ${x}^{2}+(y-2)^{2}+{z}^{2}=9$ and the vector field $F=(yz-2x)\,i+3y\,j+(x+z)\,k.$ Use the divergence theorem to find the flux of $F$ across $S.$
question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(yz-2x)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(3y)+\frac{∂}{∂z}(x+z) \\  & =-2+3+1 \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

Let $R$ be the solid sphere of radius $3$ enclosed by $S.$ Then, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS & ={∭}_{R}2\,\text{d}V \\  & =2{∭}_{R}\,\text{d}V \\  & =2\cdot \text{Volume}(R) \\  & =2\cdot \frac{4}{3}\pi \cdot {3}^{3} \\  & =72\pi .\end{aligned}
$$
